result:
## 1. The reading of his words
- Fair as a first test: nothing is built or picked, the weightings are named, a hit is one sample, and the claim is a rate.
- It leaves out scale. "Statistically hit" suggests a very large number of tries; this is about 280,000 growths of 8 rounds per weighting of takes. Give the bound in those terms.
- It leaves out "need". The study can say whether sampling hits a copier, not whether a copier can only be hit.
- It leaves out what follows a hit: whether the two left are met and doubled again. Only DC 5.3 touches this.
- It leaves out many separate origins meeting at random (see 2), and a copier of whatever it meets (CC-2 asks for only two forms).
- "A case is one sample; a copier is a rate" blurs pattern and weighting. A copier is a pattern; how often the growth makes one is a rate under a weighting.

## 2. The soup
- Fair only if said plainly: every pattern that meets is descended from one supplied start of three to five knots. The meetings are made by the law's takes, not by mixing.
- Not an arm here: there is no scratch, the cost is unknown, and STEPS-1 already gives many pairs.
- Register it by name as a later ticket, and say in the claim that it is not read here.
- Smallest form: two census starts, each sampled under the census weighting, joined at round 0 by one new shared distinction between one uniformly sampled knot of each.
- That is a new weighting of connected starts of six to ten knots, not a new rule of the growth, so the law is untouched and the C-S1 argument applies.
- What must be said: "the round-0 meeting is supplied by the weighting; every later meeting is made."
- Meetings supplied at random during the growth are a supplied rule of the law's kind: a separate ticket, with the owner's leave.

## 3. C-S1, the renaming argument
- **Rations.** FLOOR1, FBP, CAP-2/3/4, ORD and RATION-2 are functions of p (distinct inputs or parents) and demand D only. None uses names or the order of making.
- **Treatments, RELEASE, HOLD.** They use names only to say which usable loose distinction goes to which birth, or is kept. That is carried by a permutation of one member's usable loose distinctions.
- **The draft's reason for that step is wrong.** Such a permutation is a renaming because a loose distinction has one holder. The symmetry of the knot laws is needed only so that ties and the knot test are carried too.
- **MET and STEPS-1.** Candidates and eligibility are read at the start of the round and leave out only the birth's own inputs (FD 2.2, 2.4). One birth's take changes no other's list.
- **Takes do change other births' demand,** and so their fresh count under ORD and CAP-k. That is a fixed function of the round's takes together, so it is carried; say it.
- **STEPS-1 uses the birth record.** The induction must be on the structure with barred marks, retirement and the birth record, not "the structure". "A Markov process on structures" (PC) needs the same repair.
- **Implied births.** Each is tested against the structure before the round with its own take: carried.
- **Joins of three or more parents.** Names enter only through birth order: carried.
- **T1 and T2.** Independent takes, uniform or by holders at the start of the round. The order of the calls changes the sample, not the weighting.
- **Eight pairs sampled uniformly.** Carried.
- **Generator strings.** They name the census's chosen numbering. That changes which sample is seen, not the rate.
- **The citation is a hole.** DB 7 is stated for no taking rule and says "under a taking rule the statement fails in general". C-S1 must be its own lemma, saying why sampled takes repair it: the failure came from choosing by name.
- **The guard is unchecked.** If `pm.GUARD` counts steps of a search whose order follows names, "a round the guard stops is not read" depends on the numbering. I cannot see the engine; this must be checked or said.
- **Status.** A sound outline for all 84 laws and both swaps, unrefereed, and not written as a proof. It is checked only for T1 under MET, through round 3, on 36 starts.
- **The check is thin.** 192 of the 425 checks had a single history, so they tested nothing about takes.
- **What the result may say:** "argued for every law of the family; checked exactly on small starts through round 3 and by sample at 8 rounds". Not "cannot recur".
- **R7 and R8 must add:**
  - shifts of the order of distinctions (the sister study's defect), and knots alone and distinctions alone;
  - T2, HOLD, and STEPS-1 on four-knot starts;
  - the class compared including the birth record and barred marks;
  - counts of checked histories that hold a join of three or more parents, an implied birth, two taking births in one round, and a take with two or more candidates.

## 4. C-S2, C-S3, C-S6
- **C-S2: right.** Every ration gives a one-parent birth at least two fresh distinctions, so no two-place knot arises. It rests on ticket A's S2 with three or more holders, which is unrefereed. Check ties on the three- and four-knot starts.
- **C-S3: has a gap.** By D 2.6, X's own members are "descended from X only", and one of them can be an offshoot of a start knot holding two.
  - Under CANCEL-WAIT (and HOLD) such a member can wait and sit in one of the two parts; the reading asks only that one member of each part be made after round s.
  - It is proved for CANCEL-RETIRE and CANCEL-OFFSHOOT with RELEASE, where every member after round t was made in round t.
  - PC6 is "by argument" for those four laws and "check" for COPY-LAW(CANCEL-WAIT).
- **C-S6: right.** It leaves open only the soup of section 2.

## 5. The rate rule
- **It does not test the meeting.** It tests Y making births. Y barred can still be taken from, and nothing masks joinability. Either add FD 5.6's masked continuations at confirmation, or rename the case (see 14).
- **"Needs" is the wrong word.** D 4.2's "needs Y's births" means none in B(i). Here a case with 3.3% against 8.3% would "need" the meeting. Use "met more often with Y", and keep "needs" for zero of 1,000 in both controls.
- **From both: the Y-barred control is empty.** With Y barred nothing is descended from Y, so q₀ = 0 by construction and only q_Y tests anything. Say so. This is the same defect the drafter found in ticket A's values reading.
- **The events differ.** q₁ is read after the meeting; q₀ at any round after s. With nothing barred the knot limit is also reached sooner. Both lean toward the negative.
  - Keep the test as it is and say so.
  - Also report q₁ at any round after s.
  - Fix how a stopped continuation is counted.
- **The test to register.** One-sided Fisher exact on each 2×2 table (met or not; nothing barred against the control). Both must pass, with no split of the level between them.
- **Sharing the level.** One family for the ticket: m is every discovery of the claimed readings over R1, R2, R5 and R6, counted before any confirmation. The reported readings get their own family.
- **Family-wise, not false-discovery rate.** One confirmed case overturns PC3.
- **Minimum difference.** None required; report the difference with its interval. State the power: at 100, a discovery needs about 7 of 100 against 0, so a zero speaks only of cases about ten points over a zero control.
- **Is the 0.01 claim true?** Only with these repairs:
  - the null is "q₁ not greater than both", not "do not differ";
  - m must be defined (do ticket A's values cases count?);
  - it is per run, so about 0.03 or more over the ticket;
  - the K′ = 300 swap uses i = 100 to 299, which are confirmation indices; give it its own strings.
- **Shared strings.** `|BN|s|i` is shared by every pair of a round. That is harmless under Bonferroni; say it.

## 6. The zero bounds
- **Census weighting, every start read:** the arithmetic is right.
- **Labelled weighting:** the inequality is right, but under parity Σw and max w must be over the 3,344 starts read, not 257,303.
- **Not-all-equal:** this is a stratified sample, not "M growths". Five-knot starts are 93.5% of the census weighting and 98.9% of the labelled one, so the bound is about 3/300 = 1% under each. Sampling without replacement is no worse.
- **Registered design:** repeats get fresh strings, so nothing is counted once.
- **Scratch:** counting repeats once breaks the labelled weighting, and "this sample's weighting" names no weighting. Restate the scratch bounds by stratum.
- **Each bound is separate.** For all 84 laws at once use about 7.4/M.
- **No bound on "share of met pairs".** Pairs of one growth are not independent.
- **Honest sentence:** "No growth held a confirmed case. Under [weighting], the rate of growths holding a case our test can see is below 3/M at 0.95, each law separately. Smaller differences are not bounded."

## 7. The readings
- **Form:** keep. Add D 5.1's condition 3: Y's form is not X's form. Otherwise X leaving two of its own form counts as a case.
- **Values by X:** claim it strictly, both from X only. Report the from-both variants apart; q₀ cannot see them.
- **Ticket A's values reading:** the strict reading was defined after the looser one was seen to pass. Disclose that, and give ticket A's reading its own stated verdict rather than a footnote.
- **Wholly apart:** keep; without it "the meeting" is undefined. Report how many pairs it removes under STEPS-1.
- **"X always made":** enforceable for members. But at s = 1, X's members are children of start knots, so X's form is one round from the supplied start. Report cases by s.
- **DC 6 and claim §7 disagree** on whether Y holding start knots can be "made". Fix one.

## 8. CC-2
- A fair shape: one made form, several second forms, seen again.
- **The thresholds are arbitrary.** 0.6% is back-figured from "3 of 100", and is the two-sided lower end.
- **Register instead:** at least 3 of 100 fresh growths of the start, each holding a confirmed (F, G) case, with stage 2's own Bonferroni family. Report the rate with its interval. No named percentage.
- **Undefined:** growths or cases; each start or pooled; the stage-2 level.
- **"Not of the others"** must be rates per met pair (F, G′) with a one-sided test, not raw counts.
- **A248.** I do not have its text. "Some and not all" needs a G′ that F met often enough to bound its rate. Otherwise "not for others" is only low power.

## 9. The family and the swaps
- No weighting of laws: right.
- STEPS-1 was added after the scratch. It favours a positive and is disclosed: fine.
- What a critic would say leans negative:
  - the strict values reading was defined after the looser one passed;
  - q₁ is read "after the meeting" against q₀ at "any round";
  - s is at most 4, with 8 rounds and 500 knots;
  - the built-structure reading is dropped;
  - HOLD and STEPS-2, where the scratch came nearest, run on small starts only.
- Cheap repair for the last: run HOLD and STEPS-2 on the 300 five-knot sample under parity.

## 10. The knot test
- **Mark them, and give every rate twice:** over all growths, and over growths with no failing knot. The second is a conditioned weighting; name it.
- **A case in a growth with a failing knot** is reported marked and does not count toward CC-1 or CC-2.
- This agrees with D 8 ("reported, marked") and FD 7 ("a birth with a fresh distinction need not pass").
- I cannot check the frozen predictions of tickets A and B; they are not in what I was sent.
- **Classify all failures,** not 25: kind, number of parents, took or not, implied or not, round.
- **PC12** ("every law") is over-pinned.
- **Continuations:** by S1 a failing knot stays failing, so testing at the last round is enough. Say why.

## 11. Cost
- Fair if said: "under not-all-equal the five-knot starts are sampled, once each; the bound there is 1%, about twenty times weaker than parity's."
- **Keep 8 rounds.** Six rounds changes the event read; fewer starts only widens a stated bound.
- **Register the order of running** (the sample list's own order), so a stop for cost leaves a prefix that is still a sample.

## 12. The definitions
- **Continuations.** The state must include the birth record, the bars and the round number. Say they run through round 8, and what a stopped one counts as.
- **"Y's own"** allows any descent, so a third part's forms count, and so does Y itself waiting. Require descent from Y only and a member made after round s.
- **T2** has no stated call. Give it.
- **Generator strings.** No exact tokens for ration and knot law, no order of suffixes, and no place for `|S2|`.
- **R8** needs its own strings, or its samples are neither paired nor independent.
- **The labelled weighting** is by knot numberings only; say so.
- **Stage 2 and m:** undefined, as in sections 5 and 8.
- **"Seeds"** (D 9) and "generator strings" are two words for one thing.

## 13. The predictions
- **True by implication:** PC4.
- **Over-pinned or expected to fail somewhere:**
  - PC1: 5% against 4.5% seen, at other bounds and with another mix of starts.
  - PC5: "no discovery" among perhaps a thousand cases; say "none confirmed".
  - PC10: "each law", where pairs are a few per thousand.
  - PC12: "every law".
  - PC3b: "under no other law".
- **Ill-defined:** PC9. The rates are correlated and many are zero. Register one statistic per law with an exact test.
- **Marked "seen" but not run:** PC3 for STEPS-1 on five-knot starts and under not-all-equal.
- **PC6:** see section 4.
- **PC13:** not seen under STEPS-1.
- **Missing:**
  - a positive control for the rate rule. R0's two values confirmations serve for values; form has none. Ticket A's designs under sampled takes would give one, and would tie A to C.
  - a prediction for from both;
  - the scale sentence of section 1.

## 14. Words
- **A case:** keep.
- **A case that needs the meeting:** replace (see section 5).
- **Discovery / confirmation:** replace with "passes at 100" / "confirmed". "Found" is already used by "candidate found".
- **A candidate found:** replace with "a candidate seen again".
- **A case with no measured rate:** false, since it has one. Use "a one-history case", with its numbers.
- **Values by X:** clashes with D 2.6's "made by X" (at least one). Use "values, both from X".
- **W1, W2:** clash with DB's W1 to W4, the start's meetings. Use the names: census, labelled, take-by-take and holder weighting.
- **The null pairs:** replace with "the unmet pairs".
- **The continuations of a pair; a sampled growth:** keep.
- **"Hit" and "soup":** only in his quotation and in the form 'his "hit", read'. The report's bare "soup" must not enter the texts.
- **Other breaks:**
  - "draws" (PC), banned by DC 0;
  - "one component frozen" (PC), where "frozen" is the glossary's word; say "barred";
  - "the meeting hands Y's value"; in D 3.4 it is a birth that hands on;
  - "the growth holds two patterns"; knots hold;
  - "nearly every round" (claim §2) with no weighting named beside it;
  - "would be a template replicator"; say "the nearest term in that literature".

## 15. The eight open questions
1. Yes in shape; see section 5. No minimum difference; state the power.
2. Family-wise, one family for the ticket.
3. Claim the strict reading. From both does not count as from X. Ticket A's reading gets its own verdict.
4. Keep wholly apart.
5. Keep 8 rounds with fewer starts.
6. Mark them, give rates both ways, and do not count them toward the claims.
7. A later ticket, as a weighting of starts.
8. The same start for "seen again". Also report, from R1, how many starts make F and meet G under the census weighting.

## 16. Scope and honesty
As I would write it for him:
- "We built nothing. Each of 84 laws grew every small start with every take left to chance, and we counted."
- "We expect to find no pattern that leaves two of what it meets more often than the law leaves two without it."
- "That would bound the rate, under each named weighting, at about 1 growth in 2,000 for cases large enough for our test to see. It would not show a copier cannot be hit: these are thousands of short growths from starts of at most five knots."
- "One thing is found: under one law, after a meeting, Y's value sits at two loose made places more often than without it, one from X and one from Y. That is made by both; it is not a copier."

Sentences in the drafts that say too much:
- "CC-1 fails everywhere": say "not found; bounded".
- "Cannot recur" and "no longer threatens a result".
- "Every MET form case is the law's own": say "none was shown to be met more often with Y".
- "X does not leave two of it more often…": that is two cases.
- "Every start of up to five knots read": not under not-all-equal.

## 17. Verdict
Freeze after listed changes.

**Required, in order:**
1. Repair the rate rule: masked control or rename; "needs"; the from-both control empty; events and stopped continuations fixed (5).
2. C-S1 as its own lemma, with the state named and the guard checked; R7 and R8 widened with coverage counts; the wording "argued and checked" (3).
3. Values: strict claim, from both apart, ticket A's reading with its own verdict, the post-hoc choice disclosed (7).
4. Y's form not X's form (7).
5. The error family, the index overlap, the stage-2 level, and the power sentence (5, 8).
6. The C-S3 gap and PC6 (4).
7. Zero bounds: strata, set-aside weights, no bound on pairs, the scratch restated (6).
8. Knot test: both rates, every failure classified (10).
9. CC-2 made definite (8).
10. Words (14).
11. Predictions repaired, and a positive control added (13).
12. The soup sentence and the named later ticket (2).
13. The definition gaps (12).

**Optional:**
- HOLD and STEPS-2 on the five-knot sample.
- q₁ at any round, reported.
- Ticket A's designs under sampled takes.
